title: How many times heavier is a sumo wrestler?
description: Five sumo wrestlers and six ballet dancers are weighed. The video finds one typical weight for each group with the mean, and compares the two means to answer how many times heavier a sumo wrestler is.
teaching_notes: One idea: groups of different sizes are compared through their means, not their totals. Watch for students who divide the two totals instead of the two means.

source: Weights of sumo wrestlers and ballet dancers: about how many times heavier is a sumo wrestler
video_script.why: The child can find a mean and now uses two means to answer a how many times question.
video_script.substitution: Share each group's total among its own members, then divide one mean by the other.
video_script.payoff_line: A sumo wrestler is about six times as heavy as a ballet dancer.
maths_rules: check: 5 x 42 = 210 and 6 x 42 = 252; 240 is nearer to 252
video_script.design: One idea: compare groups of different sizes by their means. Two groups of weight cards sit in the anchor; each is shared into equal boxes on the board, and the two means are set side by side.

<bookmark mark='m4'/>About how many times heavier is a sumo wrestler than a ballet dancer?

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: To find: how many times heavier a sumo wrestler is

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find how many times heavier a sumo wrestler is.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, add the five sumo weights.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>They make one thousand two hundred and one point nine kilograms.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Shared among five wrestlers, the mean is two hundred and forty point three eight kilograms.

marks.m1: the six ballet weights are added to 254.5
marks.m2: 254.5 is shared into six equal boxes

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, add the six ballet weights.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>They make two hundred and fifty four point five kilograms.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Shared among six dancers, the mean is about forty two point four two kilograms.

marks.m1: the two means are placed one over the other

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, ask how many ballet means fit into the sumo mean.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>That is the sumo mean divided by the ballet mean.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check with round numbers.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Five times forty two is two hundred and ten.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Six times forty two is two hundred and fifty two.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Two hundred and forty is nearer to two hundred and fifty two.

marks.m2: the value 5.67 is rounded up to 6

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A sumo wrestler is about six times as heavy as a ballet dancer.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The exact division gives five point six seven, which is close to six.
